## 2. Target architecture options

### A. Same repo, same process, hard module boundary + host adapter (today)
- What changes: nothing structural. Finish ratchets: reverse-import guard (done), UI->lib/db guard, route handlers use host.* only.
- Risks: boundary erodes by convention; the Cyrus UI keeps shipping with Nxeon deploys and an Nxeon outage is a Cyrus outage; cannot scale or restart independently; one Next build for ~8,300 files.
- Migration: none. Rollback: n/a.
- Deploys: unchanged (one promote, one blue/green); cyrus.my vhost unchanged; auth unchanged (bridge inside one app); cost: zero extra.
- Verdict: a safe floor, not an end state. It does not answer "separate app".

### B. Same repo, separate Next.js app and process (cyrus-web), own worker, shared Postgres with schema/role separation
- What changes: apps/cyrus (own next.config, layout, globals, middleware) importing lib/cyrus via a package alias; app/dashboard/cyrus, app/api/cyrus, app/cyrus-host, app/admin/cyrus*, app/(marketing)/mods/cyrus move to it; Nxeon keeps thin entry points (NxLabs cards, server banner, Stripe webhook hook) that call lib/cyrus-client. cyrus-web.service on its own port; cyrus-worker.service; Cyrus tables move to schema `cyrus` with role `cyrus_app` (no grants on Nxeon tables; Nxeon role loses Cyrus tables) in the same Postgres; own .env.
- Risks: the 123 UI files must stop importing lib/db/auth first (the real work); shared UI primitives need a package or a copy; two builds on node-2 (more build-lock contention); shared Postgres means a noisy neighbour is still possible; middleware split must be exact or cyrus.my 404s.
- Migration: see M1-M8. Rollback: nginx upstream flip back to nxeon_web (the old routes stay mounted but flagged until soak ends); DB schema move is `ALTER TABLE .. SET SCHEMA`, reversible in the same transaction; keep search_path fallback.
- Deploys: promote-cyrus.sh armed (already written: staging first, side-port smoke, atomic symlink, auto rollback, worker after web); a Cyrus-only change no longer restarts nxeon-web; Nxeon promote unchanged. cyrus.my vhost: change upstream to 127.0.0.1:<cyrus port>; admin host the same. Auth: bridge flows stay (cookie already separate), but Cyrus stops reading Nxeon's session table: it verifies the assertion and holds its own session row. Cost: one more Next process (~1-2 GB RSS), one more build slot; no new servers, no new DB.
- Verdict: recommended.

### C. Fully standalone product: own DB, OIDC SSO, Nxeon API client for installs/servers/billing
- What changes: B plus own database instance, own host(s) (plan says own VPS pair + build host behind Cloudflare), OIDC from Nxeon as IdP, host.http adapter only (already built), wallet charge via Nxeon API (or own Stripe), object storage/CDN, own monitoring and backups, own admin.
- Risks: data cutover with write freeze (28 to 50 tables, no FKs helps); Stripe customers/subscriptions live in Nxeon's account (split-brain on refunds, chargebacks); install state in ServerMod/GameMod needs an Nxeon-side install API contract hardened; region latency (primary Singapore, node-2 Germany); ops burden (2nd stack to patch, back up, monitor); legal (separate ToS/Privacy).
- Migration: B, then P5 data split rehearsal, P7 infra move. Rollback: repoint DNS + DB dump restore within the soak week (runbook CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md). Deploys: independent pipeline fully; cyrus.my goes to its own origin; auth: pure OIDC/assertion, no shared session table; cost: new servers (~2 boxes), Cloudflare/R2, plus ongoing ops time.
- Verdict: a valid end state only if there is a business reason (sell/partner Cyrus, separate ops team, scale). Do not start here; B makes C a deployment exercise rather than a rewrite.

## 3. Recommendation and milestones
Recommend **A now -> B -> C only when a reason appears**. Each milestone ships on its own, behind a flag or a ratchet, and is reversible.

| M | Ships | Needs owner? | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 (this branch) | self-reporting report script, reverse-import ratchet, 6 pure modules behind lib/cyrus | no | revert commit |
| M2 | Reverse hotspots collapsed to 3 declared entry points: lib/auth.ts/app/layout/login stop importing lib/cyrus/bridge/config (inject via a tiny nxeon-side `lib/cyrus-entry.ts`), Stripe webhook calls host hook, worker/game-mods + mod-health via registry | no | revert |
| M3 | UI ratchet: Cyrus routes may not gain imports of lib/db, lib/auth, lib/settings (forward baseline for app/components, 123 files); then convert routes in batches to `getHost()` calls (auth via host.auth, db via cyrusDb/host.users). Each batch tsc + route tests | no | per-batch revert |
| M4 | Decide the status of lib/modbuilder + lib/cyrus-mods impure files: declare `lib/cyrus/nxeon-wiring` (host-side, own baseline) or push db calls behind host.*; update ~20 tests that read them by path | no (pure refactor) | revert |
| M5 | Shared UI package (packages/ui or components/ui re-export) used by both; Cyrus own shell + globals | owner reviews visuals | flag |
| M6 | cyrus-worker unit (registerCyrusSweeps only), same repo, same DB | no (ops) | restart nxeon-worker with sweeps back |
| M7 | apps/cyrus Next app + cyrus-web unit + port, cyrus.my upstream flip on staging first; promote-cyrus.sh armed on staging | owner arms prod (CYRUS_ARMED_FILE) | nginx upstream flip |
| M8 | DB schema/role split inside the same Postgres; own migrations | owner approves SQL | SET SCHEMA back |
| M9 (optional, C) | own DB instance + hosts, OIDC, own admin host | yes (all decisions) | DNS + restore |

M1-M4 are agent work with no owner input. M5-M8 need single-agent, run-alone sessions (physical moves), per the tracker rule.

## 4. What I changed on the branch
- `scripts/cyrus/separation-report.ts`: the table above from code (imports both ways incl. lists, Prisma ownership, settings/env, worker, targets.json modes, nginx upstream, cookie, Stripe, design-system edges); `--json`, `--lists`.
- `test/cyrus-reverse-imports.test.ts` + `test/fixtures/cyrus-reverse-imports-baseline.json`: fails on any NEW Nxeon -> Cyrus import and on stale baseline entries (regenerate with UPDATE_CYRUS_REVERSE_BASELINE=1). Baseline today 32 files / 59 pairs.
- Moved (git mv + one-line re-export shim at the old path, importers untouched): lib/cyrus-mods/{community,icon-html,rescan,tested,game} -> lib/cyrus/mods/; lib/modbuilder/studio-decision -> lib/cyrus/builder/. The seam baseline did not need to change (these files had no Nxeon imports).
- docs/DOCUMENTATION.md change-history entry.
- **Deliberately NOT done (risk)**: moving the coupled lib/modbuilder + lib/cyrus-mods files (create, install, delivery, modpack, store, access, config-delivery, meshgen, designer-ship; pages, registry, social, installed, featured, gate, media, seo, listing, remix). The L2 plan said "relocate into lib/cyrus", but 16 of them import lib/db/settings/auth/rate-limit/sandbox/mods; moving them would add ~25 pairs to the lib/cyrus seam baseline (the ratchet goes up, not down), and about 20 tests read them by path (test/cyrus-storage-accounting, cyrus-game-slots, cyrus.test, cyrus-planner ...). They are really the Nxeon-side route composition root. M4 is the proper treatment. Also not done: listing.ts (imports lib/mod-markdown, shared with Nxeon mod pages), remix.ts/seo.ts/media.ts (depend on non-moved siblings).

## 5. Verification
- `scripts/devhost tsc`: clean.
- Cyrus + modbuilder suites via devhost: see result line appended below by the architect run (test/cyrus-*.test.ts, test/modbuilder*.test.ts).
- Not run: next build, any deploy.

## 6. Owner decisions needed
1. **Billing owner**: Nxeon as the only payment provider (wallet debits via API; Cyrus never touches Stripe; recommended, already the coded default) vs Cyrus' own Stripe account (adapter built, split-brain risk on existing subscriptions/refunds). Blocks M-C and removes the 6 Stripe imports.
2. **SSO model**: Nxeon as IdP forever (recommended; assertion flow built, one account, one wallet) vs Cyrus own accounts at launch. Decides whether Cyrus keeps any session table of its own.
3. **Domain and cookies**: stay on cyrus.my with host-only `__Host-` cookies (current; users re-login once on cutover) and keep /mods/cyrus SEO via 301 or serve it from Cyrus; admin host (CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST) on its own name.
4. **Database**: same Postgres with own schema + role (M8, recommended next) vs own instance (C). Also own Anthropic credentials/budget vs shared.
5. **Process split**: approve the "B" direction (a separate cyrus-web process and worker on the same box) so M5-M8 can be scheduled as run-alone sessions.
6. Hosting for C (own VPS pair, region) and whether Cyrus is meant to be sold/partnered; if not, stop at B.

```
 build service .... services/modbuilder (Docker on VM 88001): Claude CLI -> javac -> scan -> jar
 flight hosts ..... node-2: Test Flight (throwaway Paper), meshgen/Blender sandbox, sound render, Try It controller
 data ............. Postgres (Cyrus* tables via cyrusDb), object stores (packs, library), staging disk /tank/cyrus-library-staging
```

Rule of the layers: pure modules (`lib/cyrus/**` marked "PURE, client-safe") hold schemas, validators, planners and simulators; anything that touches the network, disk, DB or a subprocess is "SERVER ONLY" and reached through injected dependencies, so the same logic runs in unit tests, on node-2 flights and in production.

## The host seam (direction A: Cyrus needs things FROM Nxeon)

`lib/cyrus/host/` defines small interfaces; inside Nxeon `host/nxeon.ts` answers them with the existing Nxeon code unchanged. Moving Cyrus out means giving it a different answer to the same interfaces (`host/http.ts`, an HTTP client for Nxeon's Platform API).

| Interface | What Cyrus asks for |
|---|---|
| `settings` | read/write Settings (`cyrus_*` keys), stored-value helpers |
| `rateLimit`, `audit` | rate limiting and the audit log |
| `auth` / `access` | current/real user, `requireArea`, `canAccess`, preview-account list |
| `users`, `jobs`, `servers`, `records` | platform tables Cyrus must not read directly (97 call sites to 0, enforced by tsc) |
| `installs` | engine install/uninstall of prefetched packages, state path, `openFiles` |
| `builds` (r34) | the build engine (`ModBuild` store) |
| `mods` (r34) | mod pages |
| `billing` (r34) | money: Stripe containment + wallet (default provider = Nxeon; an own-Stripe adapter is built but unused) |
| `db` | the typed `cyrusDb` accessor: only Cyrus' own tables + `$transaction`/raw SQL |

Ratchets (tests that stop the coupling growing): `test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts` (Nxeon imports under `lib/cyrus`: 74 -> 40 -> **5**, all client-safe/pure and copied on move day), `test/cyrus-db-seam.test.ts` (no Nxeon-table access), `test/cyrus-db-split.test.ts` (Cyrus-table call sites outside `lib/cyrus` must use `cyrusDb`; r37 found 338, r43 moved them all: baseline now empty). Detail and the move plan: [CYRUS-PLATFORM.md](../CYRUS-PLATFORM.md), [CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md](../CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md).

## The Nxeon <-> Cyrus bridge (both directions)

```
 Direction A: Cyrus -> Nxeon (host seam / Nxeon Platform API v1, served BY Nxeon)
   identity, wallet/Stripe, entitlement, list servers, inventory, write mod files (hash preconditions), reload/restart, logs, set pack
 Direction B: Nxeon -> Cyrus (Cyrus API v1 + signed webhooks, served BY Cyrus)
   projects, builds, catalog, installs, personal API keys; webhooks: build.finished, mod.published, install.result, ...
 Both sides: Ed25519 signed assertions with a STABLE subject id (never email), service tokens cyk_<id>_<secret> (only sha256 stored), idempotency keys, audit.
```

- **API v1** (`lib/cyrus/api/v1`, `app/api/cyrus/v1`, flag `CYRUS_API_V1`): OpenAPI 3.1 generated from the Zod schemas (`docs/api/cyrus-v1.openapi.yaml`, see [reference/openapi.md](reference/openapi.md)); read slice, 6 write endpoints, 5 signed webhooks with a transactional outbox, retries and dead letter. The Nxeon-side client and receiver are in `lib/cyrus-client` (imports nothing from `lib/cyrus`).
- **Platform API v1** (`lib/nxeon-platform`, flag `CYRUS_PLATFORM_API`): per-server **grants** a user gives Cyrus on a consent screen (`servers.read`, `inventory.read`, `files.write.mods`, `server.reload/restart`, `logs.read.tail`, `pack.set`), call audit, rate limits, hash-checked file changes; entitlement mirror (fail closed); Nxeon -> Cyrus events with an outbox (`server.version_changed`, `server.deleted`, `grant.revoked` ...).
- **Domain mode** (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, r36): one app serves `nxeon.cloud/dashboard/cyrus` (portal chrome) and `cyrus.my/...` (Cyrus chrome); Sign in with Nxeon / Sign in with Cyrus land on the same account; single logout both ways. Detail: [05 bridge and accounts](05-bridge-and-accounts.md).

## Target architecture and monorepo / deploy plan (r37, scaffold only)

```
 cyrus.my (landing, Cloudflare)    app.cyrus.my (customer app)     admin.cyrus.my (Cyrus admin)
              \                          |                         /
               +--- Cyrus services: API (api.cyrus.my) + workers + own DB + object storage/CDN + build service
                              |  ^
        Cyrus -> Nxeon:       |  |   Nxeon -> Cyrus:
        Nxeon Platform API    v  |   Cyrus API v1 + signed webhooks
                          nxeon.cloud (portal, billing, game servers, admin)
```

Principles: Nxeon = identity + money + game-server hosting; Cyrus = everything about mods; one account, one wallet, one Stripe; the browser talks straight to the service that owns a feature; every cross-app call is a versioned, tested contract; every phase flag-gated and reversible. Phases P0..P8 (decisions, front door, Cloudflare for Nxeon, extract the Cyrus app into a monorepo, bridge hardening, data split, portals, infra move, launch gate) are in the plan file `CYRUS-FULL-PLAN.md` (agent-notes, summarised in [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md)).

Monorepo (r37): `platform/targets.json` + a generated dependency map (`docs/cyrus-platform-depmap.md`), `scripts/platform/affected.mjs`, `apps/cyrus-site` (the static landing with atomic publish/rollback), `scripts/ship <nxeon|cyrus|site|all>`, `scripts/promote-cyrus.sh` (dry-run capable, **not armed**). **No source file has been moved**; physical extraction into `apps/` is a later, single-agent job after the r38-r45 work merges.

## Data flow: a build

```
 prompt -> lib/cyrus/prompt-check (gibberish refused before tokens are held)
        -> lib/cyrus/route + engine-core/router (what artifact does this need? honest limits, plan gate, fail closed)
        -> tokens: reserve  (lib/cyrus/tokens, cost caps, kill switches)
        -> lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild -> build service POST /builds (tier -> model, images, ModSpec, assets, designs, catalog tools)
              service: Claude CLI (Read/Write/Edit only) in a throwaway workspace -> precheck -> javac --release N vs pinned Paper API
                       -> autofix / repair (<=3, cheap-first, escalate after 2) -> bytecode+source scan -> jar (reproducible) -> release record
        -> portal: NDJSON follow stream (lib/cyrus/follow) -> studio shows live code; tokens: settle (or release on failure)
        -> optional: Test Flight gate (worker sweep) on node-2 -> verdict kept on the build; playtest bots
        -> install: delivery orchestrator (lib/cyrus/delivery) -> Mods engine -> GAME_MOD_SYNC job -> guest server (backup, staged write, rollback)
```

## Data flow: a studio edit

`studio UI -> lib/cyrus/<studio>/* pure core (validate, simulate) -> API route (session + plan gate + flag, fail closed) -> revision (immutable, 3-way merge into editor drafts) -> asset/pack builder -> next build or no-model designer build -> delivery`.

## Where to find things

- Directory map with each module's own header comment: [reference/modules.md](reference/modules.md).
- Routes: [reference/routes.md](reference/routes.md). Tables: [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md). Flags: [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md).

Full page and owner runbook: [18 SEO](18-seo.md).
148	## Continue with Google on cyrus.my (2026-10-15, branch `feature/cyrus-google-login`, NOT merged / deployed, no migration, flag `CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN`, off)
149	- **What it is.** A second path to the SAME Nxeon account: a "Continue with Google" button on cyrus.my `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` (hidden unless `CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN=1` + `CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` + `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE=1`). It uses a SEPARATE Google OAuth client ("Cyrus oAuth", Google project `cyrus-511708`) so Google's consent screen says Cyrus. nxeon.cloud's Google login and its client are untouched (the Nxeon route files do not reference Cyrus; the authorize URL is byte-identical, pinned by `test/cyrus-google-login.test.ts`).
150	- **Flow.** `GET /api/auth/google?next=` (middleware rewrites on the Cyrus host to `app/cyrus-host/auth/google`) -> sealed host-only `__Host-cyrus_google_state` cookie (state + OIDC nonce + PKCE S256 verifier + `safeCyrusNext` next, 10 min, single use) -> Google (`openid email profile`, `prompt=select_account`) -> `GET /api/auth/google/callback` (`app/cyrus-host/auth/google/callback`): state constant-time match, code exchange with verifier, id_token nonce/aud/iss/exp, userinfo `sub` equality, `email_verified` required -> `lib/google-account.findOrCreateGoogleAccount` (extracted verbatim from the Nxeon callback: link by verified email, never on unverified; signup credit/audit/partner/welcome mail) -> `createCyrusSession(user.id, null)` (the Nxeon-SSO callback's own minting path; no Nxeon parent session exists, the Cyrus session stands alone and is revocable from Settings like any session) -> private-beta rule as in `/auth/nxeon/callback` (not allowed: `/sign-in?next=` renders the beta panel).
151	- **Refused.** Suspended accounts (`account`) and non-CUSTOMER roles (`staff`, as `/auth/handoff`): staff sign in to Nxeon with a password. Every failure is a fixed code on `/sign-in?error=` (`google_unavailable|cancelled|failed|state|unverified`, plus the bridge codes), never Google text.
152	- **Limits.** 20 starts/min and 30 callbacks/min per IP (`cyrus-bridge:google-*`). Audit rows `user.login` / `user.login_denied` (`Google (cyrus.my)`), plus `user.google_link` / `user.google_register` from the shared helper; activity `auth.login` method `google-cyrus`.
153	- **Hook.** `firstRunGate()` in `lib/cyrus-bridge/google-login.ts` is a no-op where the community-username gate (`feature/cyrus-community`) attaches after login.
154	- **Owner:** runbook with the exact Google console values and the env-store command: [CYRUS-GOOGLE-LOGIN](CYRUS-GOOGLE-LOGIN.md). nginx for cyrus.my must proxy `/api/auth/google` (regex in [CYRUS-MY-LAUNCH](CYRUS-MY-LAUNCH.md)).

Edit there only and bump `CYRUS_LEGAL.version` + dates. The contact address is the Nxeon `support_email` setting. Inline `[label](href)` links; Nxeon general documents are linked absolutely (https://nxeon.cloud/legal/...), because on cyrus.my `/legal/terms` and `/legal/privacy` ARE the Cyrus documents.

Both render `components/cyrus/legal/CyrusLegalDoc.tsx`. Titles "Terms of Service — Cyrus" / "Privacy Policy — Cyrus", indexable, canonical `https://cyrus.my/legal/...`.
158	- **Google OAuth consent screen**: the Privacy Policy has a "Google user data" section (openid/email/profile only, use limited to sign-in and identifying the account, never sold, no ads, Limited Use sentence, retention and deletion).
159	- **Sitemap**: `CYRUS_LEGAL_SITEMAP_PATHS` + `CYRUS_LEGAL.lastmod` are exported for the host-aware cyrus.my sitemap. The nxeon.cloud copies are deliberately NOT in the Nxeon sitemap (their canonical is cyrus.my).

content.content:
# cyrus.my launch: host readiness (PREPARED, NOTHING APPLIED)

Status 2026-10-13, branch `feature/cyrus-portals`. This file only prepares the work: no nginx edit, env write, flag change, DNS, Cloudflare or Stripe change has been made. Every step below is for the owner (or a parent session with the owner's go) to run, in order, with the rollback beside it.

What exists today: the static landing (v7) is live on `cyrus.my` from `/var/www/cyrus.my` (nginx server block `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cyrus-my`: `/` and `/packs/p/<sha1>.zip` only, no proxy). The app already contains the whole dual-host layer (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, `lib/cyrus/bridge/*`, `middleware.ts`, `app/cyrus-host/*`); it is dormant because no request reaches the app on that hostname.

## 1. What the app does on cyrus.my (read from code)
Source: `lib/cyrus/bridge/config.ts`, `routing.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `app/cyrus-host/*`, tests `test/cyrus-bridge-routing.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-admin-host.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-portals-routing.test.ts`.

| Public path on cyrus.my | Result |
|---|---|
| `/` | nginx static landing. If it ever reaches the app: 302 `/studio` |
| `/studio[/...]` | rewritten to `/dashboard/cyrus[/...]` (the studio, Cyrus chrome) |
| `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/assets`, `/servers`, `/wallet`, `/projects[/<id>]` | customer app (`/dashboard/cyrus/app/*`), 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off |
| `/help[/<slug>]`, `/plans` | help center and plans page (read-only, 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off) |
| `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/auth/nxeon/start`, `/auth/nxeon/callback`, `/auth/handoff`, `/auth/logout` | Cyrus-host auth pages (`app/cyrus-host/*`, 404 on every other host) |
| `/api/cyrus/*`, `/api/mod-builder/*`, `/api/nxlabs/cyrus*` | the same handlers as on Nxeon |
| `/dashboard/<anything else>` | 302 to the same path on `APP_URL` (Nxeon) |
| `/login`, `/register` | 302 to `/sign-in`, `/sign-up` |
| `/mods/cyrus/*`, `/admin`, `/staff`, `/sso/*`, everything else | 404 |
| `/_next/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/.well-known/*`, `/vendor/*`, static file extensions | pass |

Gaps found while reading, and what to do about them:
1. **Community pages are not served on cyrus.my** (`/mods/cyrus` is a 404 there by design). The generated Featured mods section therefore links to `https://nxeon.cloud/mods/cyrus/<slug>` (`featured.mjs --origin`). If you want them on cyrus.my, that is a routing change plus a test, not a config change.
2. **`/api/cyrus/featured` passes** (prefix `/api/cyrus`). The landing generator reads it at build time. The landing page itself also calls `GET /api/cyrus/launch` (same prefix, anonymous) for the launch state and real plan numbers; both degrade to static private-beta wording.
3. nginx must forward only the paths the app serves (section 3) and keep everything else static, otherwise a scanner hits the app for every random path. The app 404s them anyway, so this is load, not safety.
4. The app trusts `X-Real-IP` and the LAST `X-Forwarded-For` hop; with Cloudflare in front, nginx must restore the real visitor IP (`deploy/cloudflare`, already built) or rate limits see Cloudflare's addresses.
5. No WebSocket path is exposed on cyrus.my (the Nxeon terminal and console sockets stay on nxeon.cloud). The `Upgrade` headers in the block below are copied from the Nxeon block and are harmless.

## 2. Environment (names only; set in the app's env file on the primary, then restart `nxeon-web`)
| Variable | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` | `1` | master switch; unset = nothing changes for any request |
| `CYRUS_HOSTS` | `cyrus.my,www.cyrus.my` (default) | exact hostnames that get Cyrus chrome; first entry is the apex |
| `CYRUS_ORIGIN` | `https://cyrus.my` (default) | callback and return base |
| `APP_URL` | `https://nxeon.cloud` (already set) | the Nxeon origin: identity provider, wallet, `/dashboard/*` hand-over |
| `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` | `1` | customer app + help center + plans (also needs the studio gate) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST` | `<16-63 [a-z0-9]>.cyrus.my` | secret admin host (kept ONLY in env and the password manager) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS` | optional exact staff IPs | other IPs get 404 (reads `X-Real-IP`) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY` | `1` only after the admin host works | `/admin/cyrus` 404s on every other host |
| `CYRUS_BRIDGE_REQUIRE_VERIFIED` | leave default (strict) | Cyrus sign-in needs a verified email |
| `CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN` + `CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` + `CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | `1` + the "Cyrus oAuth" client | optional "Continue with Google" on cyrus.my; default off; runbook [CYRUS-GOOGLE-LOGIN](CYRUS-GOOGLE-LOGIN.md) (needs `api/auth/google` in the nginx regex below) |
| `CYRUS_WALLET_PAY` | `1` if wallet top-ups should work from cyrus.my | optional |
| `ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_API_KEY` | optional | Economy tab live Anthropic costs (server only; not needed for launch) |

Session and SSO: no setting to change. The Cyrus session cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` (Secure, path `/`, no Domain, so it cannot be shared with or set from another host); SSO state cookies are `__Host-*_sso_state`; the callback URLs are the exact strings `https://cyrus.my/auth/nxeon/callback` and `https://nxeon.cloud/sso/cyrus/return`. Signing keys are derived from `AUTH_SECRET` unless the `CYRUS_BRIDGE_*_KEY` PEMs are set. Because cookies are host-only, signing in on cyrus.my never signs the visitor in on nxeon.cloud except through the consented SSO hop.

Also keep the pre-launch pair consistent (`cyrus_studio_public_enabled` and `cyrus_tok_live`, the smoke script checks it) and `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` for the community and featured API.

## 3. nginx additions (EXACT; add to the existing HTTPS block of `cyrus-my`, nothing else touched)
The static pieces stay: `location = /`, `/packs/`, and `location /` with `try_files`. Add one named location and proxy locations for the app paths. `nxeon_web` is the upstream already defined in `conf.d/nxeon-web-upstream.conf` and used by `nxeon-cloud`.

```nginx
# --- inside the existing `server { listen 443 ssl; server_name cyrus.my www.cyrus.my; ... }` ---
    client_max_body_size 20m;                 # attachments / images in the studio (same order as nxeon-cloud)
    error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;
    location = /maintenance.html { root /opt/nxeon/public; internal; }

    # app paths: proxied to the SAME backend as nxeon.cloud
    location ~ ^/(studio|home|new|account|assets|servers|wallet|projects|help|plans|sign-in|sign-up|auth|login|register|dashboard|legal|api/auth/google|api/cyrus|api/mod-builder|api/nxlabs/cyrus|_next|vendor)(/|$) {
        proxy_pass http://nxeon_web;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_read_timeout 600s;              # builds stream for minutes
        proxy_send_timeout 600s;
        proxy_buffering off;                  # live build streams (SSE) must not be buffered
    }
    # the favicon and the app's well-known files come from the app, not the static root
    location = /favicon.ico { proxy_pass http://nxeon_web; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; }
```
Notes:
- The landing's own assets live under `/assets/` and `/fonts`-style paths inside the static root; none of them collide with the regexp (`_next` and `vendor` are app-only).
- `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` stays on the HTTP block (certbot). Do not proxy `/.well-known/` on 443.
- Rate limits: reuse the zones the Nxeon block uses for `/login`: add `limit_req zone=nxeon_auth burst=15 nodelay;` inside a separate `location ~ ^/(sign-in|sign-up|auth|login|register)(/|$)` copy of the block above (the zone is defined in `conf.d/nxeon-security.conf`).
- Validate before reload: `nginx -t`; reload with `systemctl reload nginx` (no restart).
- A staging check without DNS: `curl -sk --resolve cyrus.my:443:<origin IP> https://cyrus.my/studio -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'`.

## 4. Cloudflare (zone `cyrus.my`)
1. SSL/TLS mode **Full (strict)** (the origin has a real Let's Encrypt certificate; the temporary self-signed one must be gone first: `openssl s_client -connect <primary public IP>:443 -servername cyrus.my | openssl x509 -noout -issuer`).
2. Always Use HTTPS on; minimum TLS 1.2; HSTS only after one week of clean traffic.
3. Real visitor IP: install `deploy/cloudflare/nginx` (CF-Connecting-IP -> `real_ip`) and the `cf-ips-update` timer BEFORE the app paths are proxied. Verify with the simulation test `test/cloudflare-realip.test.ts` and a request to `/api/cyrus/health`.
4. Cache rules (start from `deploy/cloudflare/cache-rules.json`; the list below is what this launch needs): cache `/assets/*`, `/_next/static/*`, `/packs/p/*` (immutable); **bypass** `/api/*`, `/auth/*`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/studio*`, `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/assets`, `/servers`, `/wallet`, `/projects*`, `/help*`, `/plans` and any request with the `__Host-cyrus_session` cookie. Never cache HTML of the app paths.
5. WAF: managed ruleset on; a rate-limiting rule of about 20 requests/min per IP on `/auth/*` and `/sign-in`; leave bot fight mode off for `/api/*` (the build stream and the API clients are not browsers). Do not enable "Rocket Loader" or "Email Obfuscation" (they rewrite the app's HTML).
6. WebSockets: not used on these paths. Live build streams are plain HTTP; Cloudflare closes a connection idle for about 100 s, so UNVERIFIED: confirm during the smoke that a long build's live view keeps updating (the studio polls and reconnects).
7. The secret admin host: its own proxied A record + Origin CA certificate (`deploy/cyrus/CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md`); never a per-host Let's Encrypt certificate.

## 5. Stripe (same account as Nxeon)
- Checkouts opened on cyrus.my are embedded Stripe Checkout sessions whose `return_url` is `https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/tokens/return?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` (storage add-on: `/api/cyrus/storage/return?...`), built from `returnBase`. Embedded checkout needs no return-URL allowlist.
- Dashboard: register `cyrus.my` (and `www.cyrus.my`) under Settings > Payment method domains (Apple Pay / Google Pay), same account.
- Webhook endpoint stays ONE (`https://nxeon.cloud/api/stripe/webhook`); fulfilment is idempotent and does not depend on the host. No new endpoint, no new secret.
- Customer portal / billing deep links open on nxeon.cloud (`/dashboard/*` hand-over). Plan prices in the Economy tab are display values; the charge is the Stripe Price.
- Test in test mode first: a card checkout, the return page, the token credit, then the same with the wallet (`CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`).

## 6. Order of work (each step reversible; stop at the first failure)
1. Land the branch; deploy with every Cyrus switch as today (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` unset). Nothing changes.
2. Cloudflare real-IP + SSL Full (strict) + cert check (section 4.1, 4.3).
3. Set env (section 2) but keep `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` unset; restart `nxeon-web`.
4. nginx: add section 3 to a copy, `nginx -t`, reload.
5. Smoke (section 7). Then `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP=1`, smoke again.
6. Admin host (separate runbook), then `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` last.
7. Publish the updated landing with `CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON` only when `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` is on and mods are featured.

## 7. Smoke tests (read-only)
```
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh flags     # launch pair consistent, switch combinations, env names (values hidden)
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh service   # build service reachable, auth api_key before any public launch
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh worker    # nxeon-web / nxeon-worker active, no recent cyrus errors
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh migrations
```
Plus HTTP checks (from outside, through Cloudflare):
| Request | Expect |
|---|---|
| `GET https://cyrus.my/` | 200, the static landing (same `ETag` as before) |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/packs/p/<known sha1>.zip` | 200 `application/zip`, immutable |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/studio` (signed out) | 302 to `/sign-in...` |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | 200 |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | 200 JSON |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/admin`, `/staff`, `/mods/cyrus`, `/random` | 404 |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/dashboard/servers` | 302 to `https://nxeon.cloud/dashboard/servers` |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/home` | 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off, 200 or sign-in redirect after |
| `curl -I https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | no `Set-Cookie` without a sign-in; later cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` |
| Sign in with Nxeon end to end | lands on `/studio`; Nxeon cookie NOT set on cyrus.my |
| `GET https://<admin-host>/` | 302 `/admin/cyrus` (staff only) |

## 8. Rollback
- nginx: restore the saved copy of `cyrus-my` (`cp cyrus-my.bak cyrus-my && nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`). The landing and packs are untouched by the additions, so rollback is instant and static-only again.
- App: unset `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` (and `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP`), restart `nxeon-web`: the app answers as if cyrus.my did not exist. Nxeon is unaffected throughout (separate cookie, separate hostname).
- Landing: `apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh rollback` (atomic symlink back to the previous release).
- Cloudflare: revert the cache and WAF rules you added; keep SSL Full (strict). Switching records to DNS-only exposes the origin IP and is a last resort.
- Data: nothing here writes or migrates data; the only new setting key is `cyrus_featured_pages`, `cyrus_econ_*` (projection inputs) and these can stay.
# Cyrus admin on a secret host (r51): DNS plan, protection, rotation

NOT APPLIED. Nothing here has been done to DNS, Cloudflare, nginx or the environment; the owner runs these steps.
The real hostname is a secret: keep it in the environment and the owner's password manager only, never in git, docs,
tickets, chat or screenshots. In this file it is written `<label>.cyrus.my`.

## Where the Cyrus admin is today and after this
- **Today**: inside the Nxeon admin, at `/admin/cyrus` on the Nxeon admin host (NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS), behind the Nxeon
  admin layout (staff role, staff 2FA rule, `allowed_admin_ips`) and the Cyrus preview list.
- **After**: the same pages, served on `https://<label>.cyrus.my/` (`/` goes to `/admin/cyrus`) with a slim Cyrus chrome
  (no Nxeon navigation). Staff sign in there with their Nxeon staff account (`/admin/login` on that host; the session
  cookie is host-only). During the move both work; `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` then removes `/admin/cyrus` from every
  other host (the Nxeon admin included).

## How the app enforces it (code, already on the branch)
- `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST` (env): the label must be 16-63 characters `[a-z0-9]` under the Cyrus apex; anything else is ignored.
- `middleware.ts` + `lib/cyrus/bridge/routing.ts` `cyrusAdminHostRoute`: on that host only `/admin/cyrus/**`,
  `/admin/login`, `/dashboard/settings` (staff 2FA enrolment), `/api/**` (each API authenticates itself), Next internals
  and static files exist; everything else is a plain 404. Every answer carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
- `app/admin/layout.tsx` re-checks the path on that host (defense in depth), then the usual staff checks: real staff
  account (Nxeon RBAC), no impersonation, `allowed_admin_ips`, `enforce_staff_2fa`. Each Cyrus tab checks its role area
  again through the host seam (`requireCyrusAdmin`) and the Cyrus preview list.
- Public Cyrus hosts (`cyrus.my`, `www.cyrus.my`) never serve `/admin` (404). nxeon.cloud never serves `/admin` (404,
  Nxeon's own host gate).
- `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS` (env, optional): exact client IPs; any other IP gets a 404. It reads `X-Real-IP` set by nginx;
  so port 3000 must never be reachable from outside. **Check first**: on 2026-10-11 the web process listened on `0.0.0.0:3000` (not only 127.0.0.1); confirm a host or provider firewall blocks it from the internet, or bind it to 127.0.0.1, before relying on `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS` (a direct client could set its own `X-Real-IP`). Staff sign-in is still required either way.

## DNS record plan (Cloudflare zone cyrus.my)
| Type | Name | Content | Proxy | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `<label>` | the primary's public IPv4 | Proxied (orange) | Cloudflare edge certificate covers it (universal `*.cyrus.my`) |
| AAAA | `<label>` | the primary's IPv6 (only if nginx listens on it) | Proxied | optional |
No wildcard DNS record (a wildcard would answer for every guess). Do not add TXT/CAA records that name the label.

## Certificate (the hostname must not leak)
Public certificates are logged in Certificate Transparency (crt.sh lists every name). Use a **Cloudflare Origin CA**
certificate for the origin (SSL/TLS mode Full (strict)), or a **wildcard** `*.cyrus.my` certificate. Never run
`certbot -d <label>.cyrus.my`. (Finding: Nxeon's own staff and admin hosts use per-host Let's Encrypt certificates, so
their names are already public in CT logs; consider rotating them the same way.)

## Protection options (pick one or more)
1. **Cloudflare Access** (Zero Trust, recommended): an Access application for `<label>.cyrus.my`, policy "emails in
   the staff list" (one-time PIN or the identity provider), session 8-24 h. Then nginx accepts Cloudflare ranges only
   (template option 1). The app's staff checks still run behind it.
2. **IP allowlist**: `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS` in the app (404 for others) and/or `allow`/`deny` in nginx (template option 2).
3. Always on: staff role + `enforce_staff_2fa` + `allowed_admin_ips` (Nxeon settings), noindex, no-store, no framing.

## Apply (owner, in order)
1. Pick the label: `openssl rand -hex 10` (20 characters). Store it in the password manager.
2. Cloudflare: add the DNS record above (proxied). Create the Origin CA certificate for `<label>.cyrus.my` (or reuse a
   wildcard), save to `/etc/ssl/cloudflare/cyrus-admin-origin.{pem,key}` (root, 0600 key).
3. nginx: fill `deploy/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-admin.conf.template` into `/etc/nginx/sites-available/cyrus-admin`, link it,
   `nginx -t`, `systemctl reload nginx`.
4. Env (`/opt/nxeon/.env`, production only): `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST=<label>.cyrus.my` (+ optional `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS`), then a
   normal deploy (deploy-staging -> promote-production) or a restart through the promote script.
5. Check: `https://<label>.cyrus.my/` -> admin login -> Cyrus tabs; `/admin` and `/admin/servers` there -> 404;
   `https://cyrus.my/admin/cyrus` -> 404; response header `X-Robots-Tag` present.
6. Optional Cloudflare Access (above). When staff use only the new host: `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` and restart.

## Rotation (when the name may have leaked, staff leave, or every 6-12 months)
1. New label (`openssl rand -hex 10`); DNS record (proxied); Origin CA certificate covering the new name.
2. nginx: put BOTH names in `server_name` for the overlap; reload.
3. Env: `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST=<new>.cyrus.my,<old>.cyrus.my` (comma list is accepted only for the overlap); restart.
4. Tell staff the new name through the private channel only; update the Cloudflare Access application hostname.
5. Within the hour: `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST=<new>.cyrus.my`; remove the old name from nginx; delete the old DNS record and
   revoke its Origin certificate; restart. The old name now gets no DNS answer at all.
6. Review the admin audit log (Audit & settings) for sign-ins from unknown places during the window.

## Rollback
Unset `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST` (and `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY`) and restart: the admin is back at `/admin/cyrus` on the Nxeon
admin host only, exactly as before. Removing the vhost and DNS record is optional.
# Cyrus admin on its SECRET host (r51). TEMPLATE, NOT APPLIED. Owner steps: deploy/cyrus/CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md.
# Replace __CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST__ with the real <random>.cyrus.my name (never commit the filled-in file), install as
# /etc/nginx/sites-available/cyrus-admin (+ symlink in sites-enabled), `nginx -t`, reload. Proxies to the SAME Next.js
# backend as nxeon.cloud and the Nxeon admin/staff hosts (upstream nxeon_web, conf.d/nxeon-web-upstream.conf); the app
# itself allows only the Cyrus admin on this host (middleware CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST), staff-only (admin layouts, Nxeon RBAC).
#
# TLS: do NOT issue a per-host Let's Encrypt certificate for this name: every public certificate is published in
# Certificate Transparency logs (crt.sh), which would publish the "secret" hostname. Use either
#   (a) Cloudflare proxied record + a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate (not in CT logs), recommended; or
#   (b) a WILDCARD *.cyrus.my certificate (DNS-01): only "*.cyrus.my" appears in CT logs.
server {
    listen 80;
    listen [::]:80;
    server_name __CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST__;
    location / { return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    listen [::]:443 ssl;
    http2 on;
    server_name __CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST__;
    # (a) Cloudflare Origin CA:  /etc/ssl/cloudflare/cyrus-admin-origin.pem + .key
    # (b) wildcard:              /etc/letsencrypt/live/cyrus.my-wildcard/{fullchain,privkey}.pem
    ssl_certificate     /etc/ssl/cloudflare/cyrus-admin-origin.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/cloudflare/cyrus-admin-origin.key;
    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
    ssl_ciphers HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5;

    # Never indexed, never cached, never framed.
    add_header X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow, noarchive" always;
    add_header Cache-Control "no-store" always;
    add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;
    add_header Referrer-Policy "no-referrer" always;
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000" always;
    location = /robots.txt { default_type text/plain; return 200 "User-agent: *\nDisallow: /\n"; }

    # OPTIONAL extra protection (pick what fits; docs: CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md "Protection"):
    # 1. Cloudflare only (with option (a)): accept connections from Cloudflare ranges only. Include the generated
    #    allow-list from deploy/cloudflare/ (r37), then:   deny all;
    # include /etc/nginx/snippets/cloudflare-allow.conf;
    # deny all;
    # 2. Staff IP allowlist at nginx (in addition to, or instead of, CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS in the app):
    # allow 203.0.113.10;   # example address (documentation range), replace
    # deny all;

    client_max_body_size 20m;
    error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;
    location = /maintenance.html { root /opt/nxeon/public; internal; }
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://nxeon_web;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_read_timeout 600s;
        proxy_send_timeout 600s;
    }
}

# CT: Cyrus Terms of Service and Privacy Policy (2026-10-15)

Branch `feature/cyrus-legal` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-legal`, from `main` 89608a9f). NOT deployed, no flag, no migration.
Owner paste: portal promote only.

**These are DRAFTS written from the code and docs by an engineer, not by a lawyer. A lawyer must review both documents
before public launch. Nothing here is legal advice.**

## What was built
- `lib/legal/cyrus.ts`: the single content module (version 1.0, effective/updated "October 15, 2026", `CYRUS_TERMS_DOC`,
  `CYRUS_PRIVACY_DOC`, `cyrusTermsSections(email)`, `cyrusPrivacySections(email)`, `CYRUS_LEGAL_SITEMAP_PATHS`, `CYRUS_LEGAL.lastmod`).
- `components/cyrus/legal/CyrusLegalDoc.tsx`: renderer (inline `[label](href)` links, version/effective/"what changed" hook,
  metadata helper: title "Terms of Service — Cyrus" / "Privacy Policy — Cyrus", indexable, canonical https://cyrus.my/legal/...).
- cyrus.my: `app/cyrus-host/legal/{terms,privacy}` now render the Cyrus documents (AUP and SLA stay the Nxeon documents in the
  Cyrus frame; layout footer links all four). The middleware `/legal/*` rewrite is unchanged (test pins it).
- nxeon.cloud: the same documents at `/legal/cyrus-terms` and `/legal/cyrus-privacy` (`app/legal/cyrus-*`), canonical = the cyrus.my URL.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-legal.test.ts`. Docs: `docs/cyrus/06-portals.md` (new section), `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` change history.
- Contact email = the existing Nxeon `support_email` setting (default support@nxeon.cloud), read at render.

## What the pages say (15 bullets)
1. Operator is Nxeon; Cyrus runs on the one Nxeon account; the Nxeon Terms, AUP, SLA and Privacy Policy are linked (absolute nxeon.cloud URLs) and apply; Cyrus Terms win for Cyrus.
2. Cyrus is an AI-assisted Minecraft plugin/mod generator; output can be wrong; test before production; "as is", no warranty; Minecraft is a Mojang trademark, not affiliated, no Mojang assets provided.
3. No separate Cyrus password: sign in through the Nxeon account (Google offered on the Nxeon sign-in); 18+; private beta may limit access and change features.
4. Cyrus username (creator handle) and bio are public on pages/listings/credits.
5. Tokens: units tracking measured AI cost; no cash value, not transferable, expire (date shown in account); hold then settle at actual cost; our-side failures normally not charged (fair-use limit); refused/cancelled builds can be charged; a change request is a new build; no free-refine promise; daily limits.
6. Plans/top-ups/storage sold by Nxeon, cards via Stripe, no card number stored; renewals; downgrades/cancels at period end, no partial-period refunds; refunded/charged-back purchases reverse unspent tokens; refunds follow Nxeon terms and checkout.
7. Acceptable use: no malware/backdoors, credential stealers, griefing/takeover tools aimed at others, illegal or infringing content; we scan, review, refuse, remove, suspend; scans never called "safe".
8. Ownership: you own your input; rights in output to the extent we have them; output may resemble others' and may not be copyrightable; licence to Nxeon to host/run/scan/display; you are responsible for rights in uploads; game-derived content stays private to the job.
9. Publishing: private unless published; publishing grants a non-exclusive licence to host/display/distribute/fork/remix as the listing allows; Cyrus-authored assets may be added to a CC0 community library after filters, with no credit; takedowns.
10. Third-party AI processing disclosed (currently Anthropic), with a pointer to what is sent.
11. Availability not guaranteed; features/limits/prices can change; the Nxeon SLA does not cover build results.
12. Termination, survival, liability cap (three months of payments, from Nxeon Terms), indemnity, governing law = Nxeon Terms (jurisdiction where Nxeon is established).
13. Privacy: collected data = identity (Nxeon + Google), username, prompts/uploads, generated code/assets/logs/test results, token ledger and Stripe payment status, diagnostics/IP, support messages, cookies; purposes with legal bases; no sale, no ads.
14. Google user data section: openid/email/profile only; used solely to sign in and identify the account; not sold; no advertising; no transfer except to run the service/legal; retained while the account exists, deleted with it; user can revoke in Google; verbatim Google API Services User Data Policy / Limited Use sentence with link.
15. Processors and rights: Anthropic, Google, Stripe, Cloudflare, Nxeon infrastructure and backups, email provider; transfers; cookies/consent (180 days, 30 day attribution, reject as easy as accept); retention list; export and deletion in Account > Data (7 day export link, 14 day deletion wait, what is deleted/anonymised/retained); security; 18+; changes; contact.

## Claims and code evidence
| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Sign-in is Nxeon SSO, no Cyrus password | `app/cyrus-host/sign-in/SignInView.tsx` ("There is no Cyrus password") |
| Google scopes `openid email profile`, identity only | `lib/google-oauth.ts` `GOOGLE_OAUTH_SCOPES`; callback stores `sub`, email, name, picture (`app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts`) |
| Token = measured AI cost, minimum charge, multiplier | `lib/cyrus/tokens/economy.ts tokensForCost`, `config-pure.ts` (`cyrus_tok_min_spend`), docs/cyrus/05 |
| Hold then settle; append-only ledger; expiry | `lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts` header; lots expire |
| Our-side failure free, fair-use limit, refused/cancelled charged | `economy.ts settleCharge`, `INFRA_FAILURE_CODES`; `config-pure.ts` `cyrus_tok_charge_refused/cancelled`, `cyrus_tok_free_failures` (3 / 7 days) |
| Daily caps, lower for new accounts | `cyrus_tok_daily_spend_cap`, `cyrus_tok_new_account_*` |
| Refunds/chargebacks reverse unspent tokens | docs/cyrus/05 "refunds and chargebacks reverse unspent tokens once" |
| Downgrade/cancel at period end, no mid-period refund | docs/cyrus/05 storage add-on "never a mid-period refund" (stated generally for plans; plan code not re-read, see questions) |
| Stripe, no card number stored | docs/cyrus/05 Stripe; Nxeon privacy text |
| Scanning of generated/imported code | docs/cyrus/08-security.md |
| CC0-only library, game-derived never shared, BYO private | docs/cyrus/04-assets-and-library.md legal ledger and licence rules |
| Automatic contribution after filters, opaque contributor id | `lib/cyrus/library/backend/studio-hook.ts` (HMAC contributor id), flag `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE` |
| Creator handle public | `CyrusCreator.handle` (prisma schema), erased by GDPR table |
| Build service sends prompt/project to Claude, no network for the model | docs/cyrus/01-architecture.md data flow; 08-security.md |
| Learning data is outcomes only, no prompt/code | docs/cyrus/15-learning-loop.md |
| Consent 180 days, attribution 30 days, reject-all, ad ids need marketing consent, hashed email | `lib/cyrus/analytics/consent.ts`; CyrusConversion docs |
| Cookies: `__Host-cyrus_session`, `*_sso_state` | `lib/cyrus/bridge/config.ts` |
| Export (7 day link), deletion (14 day grace) | `lib/cyrus/app/data-jobs.ts EXPORT_TTL_DAYS/DELETE_GRACE_DAYS`; UI `components/cyrus/app/AccountPanels.tsx DataPanel` |
| What erase deletes / anonymises / retains | `lib/cyrus/admin/ops.ts CYRUS_GDPR_TABLES`, `lib/cyrus/admin/gdpr.ts gdprErase` (fail closed on `CYRUS_GDPR_ERASE`) |
| Backups age out (~90 day horizon) | docs/cyrus/LAUNCH-RUNBOOK.md data-subject request |
| 18+, liability cap, wallet, governing-law wording | `lib/legal/terms.ts` (Nxeon Terms) |

## QUESTIONS the owner must decide (I did not invent answers)
1. **Jurisdiction / governing law and venue.** The Nxeon Terms literally say "the jurisdiction in which we are established ... should be finalized with legal counsel". Cyrus Terms point to it. Needs a real clause (and the legal entity name and registered postal address, which appear nowhere in the codebase; GDPR and Google verification both like a postal address).
2. **Contact email.** Using `support_email` (support@nxeon.cloud). Want a dedicated privacy@ / legal@ / abuse@ address and a DPO/EU representative statement?
3. **Refund policy for Cyrus tokens and plans.** The text says refunds follow Nxeon terms and checkout, spent tokens are not refunded, and reversal on refunds/chargebacks. ## Store the secret without echo
```bash
read -rp 'Cyrus Google client id: ' CID; read -rsp 'Cyrus Google client secret (hidden): ' CSEC; echo
cp -p /opt/nxeon/.env /opt/nxeon/.env.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
sed -i '/^CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=/d;/^CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=/d;/^CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN=/d' /opt/nxeon/.env
printf 'CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN=1\nCYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=%s\nCYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=%s\n' "$CID" "$CSEC" >> /opt/nxeon/.env
unset CID CSEC; chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env
```
